title: Siegard certification return
description: One coverage-auditor delegation's answer to a certification: whether the tests the human named would fail if a specification node's fact stopped holding. The agent returns this mapping as plain YAML text; the caller saves it verbatim, one file per node, under `siegard-reconcile/<slug>.returns/certify__<node with '/' as '__'>.yaml` — the returns are the evidence a reconciliation record is folded from. `bin/trace.py --fold` validates every return against this contract and refuses a delegation whose answer does not hold: an unusable return means the prompt was wrong, and the correction is a fresh delegation, never a repair applied to the answer by whoever saved it. It exists apart from the delivery-node contract's `coverageEntry` because its subject is a node rather than a task's criterion, and it is read by trace.py rather than by deliver.py; the state vocabulary is `coverageEntry`'s, and what each state means is defined there and applied here, never restated.

specNodeRef.description: A specification node, by identity — «Identity is the node's path from the specification root, without `.md`» (SPEC-003 R1).

certified.description: One entry per node the delegation was asked to certify — exactly that set. A node omitted reads as one that passed, and the fold refuses a return that answers for a different set than it was handed.

allOf.$comment: A certified node names the tests that certify it; a node not certified says what is unexercised, in the node's own terms. Neither answer stands without its half.

A fact read and left short of covered has a remainder, and the auditor says whether a test can close it. A covered fact has none, and a fact that could not be read well enough to look for has none the auditor can classify — `why` already says what is ambiguous, and a remainder stated over it would be a claim about a fact nobody read.

state.description: The delivery-node contract's `coverageEntry.state`, applied to a node's fact in place of a task's criterion: `covered` where the named tests would fail if the fact stopped holding — the whole test — `partial` where a stated part of the fact goes unexercised, `uncovered` where nothing exercises it, `unauditable` where the fact cannot be read well enough to look for. Only `covered` certifies; the fold writes nothing for any other state, carries the `why` into the record's notes, and carries `remainder` onto the node's entry where the auditor stated one.

remainder.description: Whether the part of the fact the named tests leave unexercised is one a test could assert — one input against one expected result — or a fact no finite test closes: an identity that spans files, the exhaustiveness of a state machine, a totality over a set nothing enumerates. Decided from the fact as the node states it, never from what the node is typed as: a `policy` naming a refusal is one input against one result, and an aggregate whose identity spans files is not. `testable` says a test can decide this node whole, so that once such a test is written and certified no judge reads the pair again; it does not say the source needs no reading for anything else. Present exactly where the state is `partial` or `uncovered`.

remainder_why.description: Where the remainder is testable, the assertion that would close it, in the fact's own terms — what input against what expected result. Where it is untestable, what no finite test asserts and why. A reader routes on this sentence: it is the test they write, or the reason they stop looking for one.

tests.description: Every test bearing on the fact, each a file the human named as proof — a test outside the named set refuses the return, because the certification is of the tests the human offered and the binding will pin exactly those. One test may bear on several facts and one fact on several tests.

file.description: The test file, spelled from the target source root exactly as the certification named it — never absolute, and never spelled from the repository around the target, the same anchor every path in a reconciliation record uses. The fold refuses a cited test the offered proof does not hold, so a path spelled another way is refused there too; stating the shape here is what keeps the contract from teaching one the record cannot carry.

name.description: The test's own name within the file, where the file holds more than one; a reader who opens the file finds the assertion by it.

why.description: What is unexercised, in the fact's own terms, or what makes the fact unauditable. "No test" is not an answer. A test that exists but cannot fail is named here, so a reader who finds it does not conclude the audit missed it.

certified.why: the refusal half is exercised; nothing in the set alters a raised invoice's amount, so the immutability the rule states over an existing invoice goes unexercised
certified.remainder_why: one input — an alteration to a raised invoice's amount — against one expected result, a refusal that leaves the invoice as it stood

certified.why: the identity is exercised at placement; nothing in the set reads an order back through billing or fulfilment, so that the same order_number names the same order across every file that holds it goes unexercised
certified.remainder_why: the identity spanning every file that holds the aggregate is a fact about where the code sits, and no finite set of reads through the entry points closes it
